facts.text: Iarnvidiur is the level-75 final of her lair with 40,000 health. She casts Iarnvidiur's Plague, Black Plague (a disease in an 850 radius lasting ten minutes), Plague Bolt and a 400-damage strike.
From half health she keeps seizing players and sending them to one of four fixed spots away from the fight.
Allakhazam lists her as a giant; a 2004 thread calls her 'she', says she regenerated faster than a 30-strong group could hurt her, and that she teleported players into the water under the bridge.
The Remnants iarn dwarves of Faraheim count the Servants of Iarnvidiur among their foes.
In the Voluspa an old giantess sits in the Iron Wood (Jarnvidr) and breeds the wolf-kin of Fenrir; Jarnvidja, 'she of the Iron Wood', is a giantess name in Snorri's lists (to verify).
facts.source: Voluspa, stanza 40 (Poetic Edda, public domain): the old one in the Iron Wood breeds Fenrir's kin

facts.text: Bot chat says she breeds two-headed wolves in the Iarnwood and is kin to the Fenris line; one grandmother's tale makes her Gjalpinulva's mother (hearsay).

story:
The old songs say that east of the world, in the Iron Wood, an old woman sits and breeds wolves: Fenrir's kin, the brood that will one day swallow the sun and the moon. The iarn dwarves of Aegir do not sing that song. They do not have to; they live beside her. Iarnvidiur is the woman of the Iarnwood, a giantess older than the island's maps, older than the dwarf clans, perhaps as old as the dead dragon under Tuscaran. Jarnvidja, she of the Iron Wood, the old lists call such a giantess. The dwarves call her the old one.

Her lair under the forest is her kennel, her nursery and her sickroom. She sits by the water under the bridge with her pups around her, the two-headed wolves and the egilvarg and the cruel grymvarg, and she licks them clean and sends them out into the iron trees to hunt, and they come back to her like dogs to a hearth. Hati and Skoll lie at her door. The dead wolf Stanga keeps the passage she set him to keep. Her herdsman Delegalt minds the giants who came to court her and stayed too long. Everything in the lair is hers, and everything in it is sick.

Because she is the plague. The black rot of the iron trees hangs around her like a cloak: her plague eats at everyone near her, her Black Plague spreads in a wide ring and lasts for many minutes, and her bolts carry it to whoever stands at range. And it closes her own wounds faster than most raids can open them. Thirty of Midgard's best stood around her in the years after the isles were found and could not get her past half.

She does not care to be fought. She looks at the raid the way a woman looks at weather. When you have hurt her badly enough to be a nuisance, at half her strength, she simply begins to put you elsewhere: she reaches out and picks one fighter after another and sets them down far from the fight, often in the black water under the bridge, the way a woman sets a pup back in its basket. Climb out, and come back, and she does it again.

Some grandmothers in Midgard say she is Gjalpinulva's mother, that she bore the dragon to the Fenris wolf before the chain closed on him, and that this is why the dragon and the two-headed wolves have the same look. The old one has never said. When she dies she says only that her brood will run when the sun is eaten. The dwarves believe her.
legend: Bring cure disease, lots of it, and a raid big enough to outdamage her healing: thirty was not enough in 2004. Shamans and healers on cure duty, nothing else. Kill Hati and Skoll at the door first. From half health she sends people away, often into the water under the bridge; climb the pillars and come back, and watch for the red cons down there. Keep a rezzer near the bridge. Don't let the fight stall or she heals back. The ring drop with parry, strength and constitution is the one everyone wants. My gran said she is the dragon's mother. My gran said a lot.

loremasterTopic.text: The woman of the Iarnwood. The old songs put a giantess in the Iron Wood breeding Fenrir's kin; the iarn dwarves live beside her and do not need the song. Her plague closes her wounds, and when you become a nuisance she sets you elsewhere, like a pup back in its basket.

bookPage: From the slate of an iarn dwarf of the Remnants, read to me in Faraheim. 'The Servants of the old one took two more of our children this moon. We went to the lair to bring them back. We found the pups first, wolves with two heads that ran to her like dogs to a hearth. She was sitting by the water under the bridge. She looked at us the way a woman looks at weather. Then she reached out, and Torvald was gone, and we heard him in the water far below, and she went back to her pups. We did not bring the children back. We brought Torvald back, which was something.'
